articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Ending Explained and the Cardinal Sin of Prequels
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ending explained: We take a look at the latest entry in the franchise and examine the cardinal sin of prequels.
body: Snow, however, was manipulated into sparing Haymitch by Jesse Plemons’ Plutarch Heavensbee, who is playing the looooong game and wants to keep Haymitch around as a potential ally to one day end the Capitol’s authoritarian reign of terror. Plutarch knew Haymitch’s loved ones would likely be taken from him; he suggested as much. But he valued a future strategic alliance more than Haymitch’s peace. (With friends like these…) Ultimately, the Games portrayed in this film act as a dress rehearsal for Catching Fire’s conspiracy to “break the Games,” which is in part the issue with this story; more on that in a bit.

In a final montage, we hear young Haymitch in voice-over, vowing to keep his promise to two women who helped draw out his spirit of rebellion. The first is Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), one of District 12’s two female tributes. She’s basically a walking middle finger to the Games and the Capitol. The second is his murdered love, Lenore, who introduced the film’s central recurring theme, “nothing is inevitable,” meaning don’t submit to a fate you don’t want just because the current system wants you to believe there’s nothing you can do about it.
points: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ending explained: We take a look at the latest entry in the franchise and examine the cardinal sin of prequels.

articles.title: 10 Near-Perfect Netflix Sci-Fi Shows That Hook You in the First Scene
articles.summary: Not every great sci-fi show starts with a bang, but the best ones grab your attention from the very first frame. Whether it’s an alien organism mutating a host in seconds, a gruesome public execution in the middle of a cultural revolution, or a child stepping into a smoke-filled battleground…
body: Spanning mind-bending mysteries, dystopian anthologies, sprawling futuristic epics, and some of the most ambitious animation on television, Netflix has delivered a fairly robust setlist of sci-fi shows over the years. With so many experiences to choose from (on Netflix and well beyond), finding that perfect sci-fi series that’s worth committing to can be quite the challenge, but the most thrilling among them make that decision easy with unforgettable premises and scientific mysteries that demand to be solved.

Opening doors to strange new worlds, fractured realities, and futures both wondrous and terrifying, these 10 near-perfect Netflix sci-fi series will pull you into the unknown from the get. Ranked from exceptional genre standouts to bona fide masterpieces, each leaves a mark that lingers long after the first scene fades to black.

articles.summary: Just like in real life, there are some people you really shouldn’t mess with in GTA 6. It’s not always easy to tell at a glance either. Books, covers, and all that.
body: GTA 6 has a wild range of NPCs with unpredictable and unique behavior — you never know what you’re gonna get. Players have been documenting their adventures across Leonida and their interactions with the locals, and have come across the weird, the funny, and the downright scary.
Not only do some NPCs fight back, but they fight hard and can take more punches to the head than Rocky. Some of them even bring little friends along to the throwdown.

The viral clip below, from @WIZZYGM, shows Lucia attempting to take someone’s car. Instead of allowing themselves to be dragged out, however, they got psyched up about having a tussle. They were into it.

Not only did they take a ridiculous number of punches directly to the nose, but at one point they even gave Lucia some free shots. Then they banged some powder up their snout and Hulked out. He even took a gunshot straight to the head!

articles.title: GTA 6’s Weirdest Cow Shows Why You Should Pause the Story Early To Explore Its Vast Map
articles.summary: I escaped GTA 6's starting neighborhood to explore the wider world, and you'll never believe what happened with this cow I found.
body: Those two chilling words were so soft I wondered if I'd heard them correctly – after all, the only souls in this orchard were me and Tootsie, an escaped cow draped in red cloth with a rosette stuck to her forehead.

But no, I had heard them, and I turned them over in my head as I led Tootsie back along her rampaging path, through fallen fruit, over a busted wooden fence, and to her owner, a dairy farmer I'd found on the side of the road, flustered and crying about his prized $2 million show cow.

I was still processing those two words as we approached the farmer's trailer, and when he told me that tonight, a fan had paid to watch a private Tootsie mud bath, I knew what I had to do. I shooed her to her freedom – "Go, run! Live your best life!" – and she galloped, ribbons fluttering, hooves pounding into the distance. To freedom rather than a busy highway, I hoped.
I was Jason, the good Samaritan (if you ignore the part where I then provoked the farmer to start a fight, knocked him out cold, stamped on his limp body and stole the $500 in his pocket).

articles.title: GTA 6 is crashing on some PS5s with error CE-108255-1 - here's what you can try
articles.summary: Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.
body: "The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. They added that other games, including GTA 5 and For Honor, run without crashing.

Another player told Dexerto that GTA 6 worked fine until Pipework, an early mission that introduces Mandy, but now crashes "every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it", which means they can’t progress.
Some PS5 Pro owners say the game crashes during the opening prologue, either at the same point every time or a few seconds in, and they haven't been able to play since launch.

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

articles.title: GTA 6 Forgot to Include the #1 Reason to Go to Actual Florida
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 's Leonida, the game's version of Florida, is a veritable cornucopia bursting with stories to uncover. You can pursue the central love story of Jason and Lucia but also go birdwatching, enjoy a game of pool, or even play multiple video games within GTA 6 itself.
body: While Disney World is based in Orlando, spread across four theme parks and two water parks. The Walt Disney Corporation has an economic impact on the entire state of Florida that seems hard to ignore in a project of this scale. According to an Oxford Economics study from 2023, the company generated over a quarter of a million jobs in the state. To put that in perspective, the report noted that this accounts for one out of every 32 jobs in Florida. Disney World also generated $40 billion in economic impact across the state.

That massive economic footprint has legislative and cultural repercussions for Florida and has since the resort opened in 1971. Experts have noted how Disney, directly and indirectly, lobbies for and against political actions across the state to serve its own interests. A very public example of this was seen when the company brought a lawsuit against Governor Ron DeSantis in 2023. For better and worse, Disney World has helped establish the culture and politics of Florida we know today. That deeply ingrained history seems like a strange thing to ignore, especially in a game so clearly about the American dream and who is allowed to control it in Florida.

articles.title: 'The Odyssey' Cast Debunks a Major Misconception About Working with Christopher Nolan
articles.summary: But according to the cast and crew of The Odyssey, there's another side to Nolan that audiences might not expect. Behind the intense focus and demanding production schedules is a filmmaker with a sharp sense of humor who genuinely loves being on a movie set.
body: Christopher Nolan doesn't exactly have a reputation for being the life of the party. The Oscar-winning director is known for meticulously constructed films, complicated narratives, and productions that demand an extraordinary amount of preparation. His movies routinely deal with weighty subjects, whether it's the nature of time, the consequences of scientific discovery, or humanity's place in the universe. Not exactly the kind of material that screams laugh riot.

Speaking with Polygon ahead of the film's home release, several members of the production shared what might surprise audiences about working with Nolan. Their answers revealed a director who enjoys a good joke, even if he isn't about to let it interfere with making a movie.

Himesh Patel, who plays Eurylochus, the second-in-command to Matt Damon's Odysseus, recalled a production that wasn't nearly as solemn as Nolan's reputation might suggest. According to Patel, Nolan's humor has a distinctly British quality.
"He's got a cutting sense of humor," Patel says. "It's that British sense of humor that can just be very sardonic. But I've always found it funny."
points: But according to the cast and crew of The Odyssey, there's another side to Nolan that audiences might not expect.
Behind the intense focus and demanding production schedules is a filmmaker with a sharp sense of humor who genuinely loves being on a movie set.

body: "I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

articles.title: Nintendo’s Long History with GTA Seems to Have Met Its End
articles.summary: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.
body: Once upon a time, Rockstar Games regularly released Grand Theft Auto games on Nintendo consoles. Exclusive ones, even. Rockstar liked having its biggest franchise available on handhelds, which has always been Nintendo’s domain. The first two games in the series got cut-down Game Boy Color editions. In 2004, Grand Theft Auto Advance for the Game Boy Advance was a canonical prequel to GTA 3. In 2013, the massive DS audience tempted Rockstar to return with a GTA 4 spinoff, Chinatown Wars.

And since then... Nothing. Well, not quite nothing. Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy — The Definitive Edition, which collects the "3D Universe" games GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas, is available on Switch, alongside every other platform known to humankind. The remasters are imperfect; the games are epoch-making. Their presence on the eShop proves that there's no inherent brand barrier, on either Rockstar's or Nintendo's side, to GTA existing on Switch.
points: Once upon a time, Rockstar Games regularly released Grand Theft Auto games on Nintendo consoles.
Rockstar liked having its biggest franchise available on handhelds, which has always been Nintendo’s domain.

articles.title: GTA 6 has a 99 Metascore from critics, but players are review bombing it
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.
body: While critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".
The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

"Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and new features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality."
points: Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

articles.title: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question
articles.summary: What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac.
body: Your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military.

Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today.
points: What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors?

articles.title: GTA 6 Transgressor locations: How to restore the first car for Wyman
articles.summary: You'll be able to start looking for GTA 6 Transgressor locations after you complete the Thrillbillies mission in Chapter 2 and collect the Vapid Dominator from Wyman (if you have the Ultimate Edition, that is).
body: He'll text to ask for help finding old wrecked Transgressors he can use to restore the classic car, which you'll then get to drive. There are three of these junks located around Port Gellhorn which you'll have to scan with the Waink It app.

The first wrecked Transgressor you can find is in a trailer park north of Sarena's Bargain Store in the middle of Port Gellhorn (you might have to zoom in to see the store). Head north, cross the road, and jump over the wall to find it there.

The second wrecked Transgressor is further north in the garage of the house opposite the Kolt & Associate's Stash House robbery (there's a metal sunflower standing in the garden, which makes it easier to recognise.) It's also to the east of Brook's Boatworks and the west of Wasteland Offroad. Head around the side of the house via the driveway to find the car in an open garage at the back.

This last one is nice and easy, behind the Dirt Merchants mod shop in the south of Port Gellhorn. Simply head right via the track that leads behind the shop, following the fence on your right and then turn left to find the wreck at the back behind the kind of trailer park area.

articles.title: Seven years on since Persona 5 Royal, Atlus says 'people won't have to wait as long as they have previously' for the next game after Persona 6
articles.summary: The amount of time it takes to develop games has been growing steadily longer for decades, and Atlus' Persona series is no exception to this rule. While Persona 4 Golden and Persona 5 were separated by four years (long considered standard for game development) it's been seven years since Persona 5…
body: Nonetheless, it's an issue that P-Studio is very much aware of, and it was recently addressed by general producer Kazuhisa Wada. In an interview with Sega Samania (via Eurogamer ) Wada stressed that the wait for whatever comes after Persona 6 will be shorter.

"Persona 6 is not the end," Wada explained. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day."

Now, we're probably not looking at a dramatic reduction in development time. Wada emphasised that "large-scale RPGs like the Personal series can take five years or more to develop," adding that. "There can be a long time between numbered entries." Yet even if the average timeline was five years, that would be a considerable improvement.

articles.title: Cheeky Malware Linked To Popular Gacha Game Cracks City Security
articles.summary: East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.
body: One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident.

Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC.

videos.title: Psycho Dead - Release Date Announcement Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: "PSYCHO DEAD" is a third-person survival horror game centered on Elixia, a mysterious girl with psychic powers, who must escape a secret laboratory infested with grotesque and monstrous creatures.
points: "PSYCHO DEAD" is a third-person survival horror game centered on Elixia, a mysterious girl with psychic powers, who must escape a secret laboratory infested with grotesque and monstrous creatures.
Explore a sci-fi setting filled with mystery and danger, where terror awaits at every corner, and discover the truth behind the horrific incident.

videos.title: [4K HDR] Grand Theft Auto 6: Digital Foundry Tech Review - The Game Of The Generation?
videos.summary: Thanks to Elgato for sponsoring this video. The Elgato 4K X and Elgato 4K Pro are essential tools in Digital Foundry's gameplay capture arsenal. Find out more here:
body: Game captured on PS5 Pro unless otherwise stated. In one of our most expansive tech reviews yet, John Linneman takes you on a tour through Vice City in Grand Theft Auto 6 in a 4K HDR video designed to capture as much of the fidelity as possible of this incredible game. Resolution and frame-rate metrics, simulation, detail, ray tracing, visual features and much, much more are covered for this once-in-a-generation game. Xbox coverage follows later today.
